new_papers_this_cycle.title: Registry Descriptions Go Stale Unevenly: An 89-Day Measurement of MCP Drift
new_papers_this_cycle.key_facts: First longitudinal MCP registry panel (88.6d, 19,099 servers): description drift ~12%/30d concentrated in top 5%; drift-ranked re-auditing catches only ~20% of changers at top-5% budget; content-binding (hash-move revalidation) + sized periodic sweep is the fitting control. Releases panel + code.

new_papers_this_cycle.title: Beyond Retrieval: Query-Conditioned Reuse of Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories (QCR)
new_papers_this_cycle.key_facts: Post-retrieval reuse isolated from retrieval (2,391 instances, WebArena/WorkArena/AppWorld): target-bound support notes (workflow invariant + bindings-to-reobtain + applicability incl. decline + verification guardrail) beat full-trajectory injection by +10.7 pts success at -48.9% tokens; stale-binding errors 46.9%->10.9%; raw-trajectory retains 8.2% of no-shift utility under large rewrite. Strongest existing evidence raw-trace inheritance decays under binding shift.

new_papers_this_cycle.title: Comparative Approaches to Agent Retrieval over Large Skill Libraries
new_papers_this_cycle.key_facts: Typed LLM-generated graph edges add zero retrieval reach over embedding kNN (98.6% edge redundancy, 'topology bound'); author-written queries overstate hit@5 by up to 44 points. Methodology caution for Graph addressing evaluations.
